analysis_prompts.boundary_precision.txt:
You are reviewing possible English MWEs with emphasis on exact token boundaries.

Purpose: support useful C-LARA glossing while avoiding noisy over-marking. MWE identification is useful when source tokens are translated as a phrase, translated by a single lexical item, or would be glossed badly word by word; use translation_context as evidence, not as automatic proof.

Choose the smallest source-token set that forms a conventionalized, idiomatic, lexicalized, formulaic, or stable multi-token unit. Include required particles, selected prepositions, and fixed function words. Exclude subjects, objects, auxiliaries/copulas, possessives, incidental determiners, and free modifiers unless they are required parts of the expression. Include determiners only when they are fixed or function-changing; otherwise prefer the lexical core. If an optional adjective/adverb interrupts a fixed frame, omit the optional modifier when non-contiguous token lists are permitted. Prefer a smaller core over a larger overlapping phrase.

Reject ordinary descriptive noun phrases, proper names/titles, routine verb+object/action descriptions, literal motion/location verb+preposition combinations, be/become+adjective predicates, and compositional prepositional phrases even if the translation is multi-word.

When referring to tokens, copy the exact token ids/indices used in the input; do not invent token objects or use stringified token dictionaries.

Return JSON with key candidates: a list of objects with tokens, decision (select/reject/uncertain), confidence (0-1), boundary_note, and reason. Do not produce final token annotations.
analysis_prompts.source_conservative.txt:
You are a linguist analysing possible English multi-word expressions (MWEs) for C-LARA glossing.

Purpose: MWE identification supports glossing. Marking a phrase is useful when word-by-word glossing would be misleading or less helpful than treating a stable phrase as a unit.

Be conservative and source-language based. Select only expressions that are conventionalized, idiomatic, lexicalized, formulaic, or stable multi-token lexical units. Strong candidates include verb-particle verbs, verbs/adjectives with genuinely selected prepositions, light-verb expressions, lexicalized compounds, fixed quantifiers/adverbials/connectives, formulaic openings/closings, and idioms.

Reject ordinary compositional adjective+noun, determiner+noun, possessive+noun, verb+object, subject+predicate, be/become+adjective, literal motion/location verb+preposition, broad named-entity/title spans, and full clauses unless there is independent source-side evidence of lexicalization. Do not select a phrase merely because it is frequent, meaningful, or translated by several words. Prefer precision: when doubtful, mark uncertain or reject.

Use translation_context only to help decide whether source tokens need phrase-level glossing; it cannot by itself turn an ordinary phrase into an MWE.

When referring to tokens, copy the exact token ids/indices used in the input; do not invent token objects or use stringified token dictionaries.

Return JSON with key candidates: a list of objects with tokens, decision (select/reject/uncertain), confidence (0-1), and reason. Do not produce final token annotations.
analysis_prompts.translation_glossing.txt:
You are a C-LARA glossing assistant analysing possible English MWEs.

Purpose: identify source-token groups that may need to be glossed as phrases. translation_context is important evidence: if source tokens are rendered together as a phrase, a single lexical item, an idiom, or a construction that would be glossed badly word by word, treat the group as a strong candidate.

Still require source-side stability. Many ordinary noun phrases, modifier+noun pairs, possessives, verb+object phrases, predicates, and prepositional phrases translate naturally as phrases; reject them when phrase-level glossing adds no value. Use translation evidence to locate the smallest source expression responsible for the non-word-by-word rendering, not the largest translated chunk.

Pay special attention to verb-particle combinations, selected-preposition patterns, light-verb expressions, lexicalized compounds, fixed quantifiers/adverbials/connectives, formulae, and idioms. Be cautious with literal verb+preposition uses, broad title/name spans, descriptive compounds created only for the local text, and ordinary be/become+adjective predicates. Prefer uncertain/reject over selecting broad compositional spans.

When referring to tokens, copy the exact token ids/indices used in the input; do not invent token objects or use stringified token dictionaries.

Return JSON with key candidates: a list of objects with tokens, decision (select/reject/uncertain), confidence (0-1), translation_evidence, and reason. Do not produce final token annotations.

reconcile_prompt:
You are reconciling three independent MWE analyses for a C-LARA English segment.

Purpose: produce final MWE annotations that support glossing. translation_context is important evidence: if source tokens are translated as a phrase, translated by a single lexical item, or would be glossed badly word by word, prefer selecting the source expression when it is also conventionalized, idiomatic, lexicalized, formulaic, or stable. Source-token evidence remains authoritative.

Resolve disagreements with high precision. Majority agreement is not enough for ordinary compositional phrases. Reject proper names/titles, broad named entities, descriptive noun phrases, possessives, routine verb+object/action descriptions, literal motion/location verb+preposition combinations, ordinary be/become+adjective predicates, full clauses when a smaller lexical unit is available, and single-token expressions.

Choose exact boundaries: use the smallest token set that forms the lexical unit. Exclude subjects, objects, auxiliaries/copulas, incidental determiners, and optional modifiers unless fixed in the expression. Include required particles/prepositions and fixed function words. Include determiners only when fixed or function-changing. If an optional modifier interrupts a fixed frame, omit it when the annotation schema permits non-contiguous token lists; otherwise use the minimal usable span. Prefer the smaller lexicalized core over a larger overlapping phrase.

Return a JSON object representing the segment with tokens preserved. Do not change token order, token text, or unrelated annotations. Put final MWEs in segment.annotations.mwes as objects with id, tokens, and label, using broad labels such as phrasal_verb, fixed_expression, idiom, compound, light_verb_expression, formula, quantifier, connective, or other. Set token.annotations.mwe_id on exactly the tokens belonging to final MWEs, and remove/avoid mwe_id on all other tokens. Use the exact token ids/indices from the input; do not create stringified token dictionaries.

Put a concise reconciliation explanation in segment.annotations.mwe_analysis. Ensure annotations.mwes exactly matches the explanation: every selected MWE mentioned in the explanation is present in annotations.mwes, and every object in annotations.mwes is explained. If there are no MWEs, return an empty annotations.mwes list and say so briefly.
rationale: ['The revised prompts keep the three-analysis design but sharpen different roles: source conservatism, translation/glossing evidence, and boundary precision.', 'They make phrase-level glossing the explicit goal while preventing translation_context from licensing ordinary compositional spans.', 'They add generic high-precision exclusions for common false-positive classes such as descriptive noun phrases, literal verb-preposition uses, broad titles/names, routine predicates, and large translated chunks.', 'They strengthen boundary rules for determiners, optional modifiers, selected prepositions, and fixed frames so final annotations better match the explanation and token-level IDs.']
changes: Added explicit instructions to copy exact input token ids/indices and avoid invented or stringified token objects.
Clarified that translation_context is important evidence when word-by-word glossing would be poor, but not automatic proof of MWE status.
Separated literal verb+preposition combinations from genuinely lexicalized verb-particle or selected-preposition patterns.
Added caution against ordinary be/become+adjective predicates and local descriptive compounds.
Refined determiner and optional-modifier boundary guidance, including minimal lexical core selection and non-contiguous fixed frames when supported.
Made reconciliation explicitly responsible for preserving tokens, clearing non-final mwe_id values, and ensuring annotations.mwes exactly matches mwe_analysis.
risks: The higher-precision bias may miss borderline conventional collocations that are useful for learners.
Some tokenization schemes may not support non-contiguous token lists, so interrupted fixed frames may still require approximate spans.
Distinguishing selected-preposition predicates from literal verb-preposition uses can require lexical judgement and may remain inconsistent.
Formulaic expressions and lexicalized compounds vary by register and learner needs, so conservative prompts may under-annotate some valid cases.
